newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli, Turkish businessmen to meet in Istanbul.
newsitem.headline: Israeli, Turkish businessmen to meet in Istanbul.

text.p: Israeli and Turkish businessmen will meet in Istanbul next month to examine how the Jewish state can penetrate markets in central Asia's Islamic republics, Israel's Export Institute said on Sunday.
Israel has sought to expand economic ties with Kazahkstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan and Azerbaijan since the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991.
"Turkey and Turkish companies can...act as an excellent bridge for Israeli economic activity in that part of the world," the institute said in a statement.

"This is mainly because Turkish companies have close and established ties in these countries...and a vast awareness of Israel's ability in fields of industry and technology which are in demand there," it said.
A spokesman said the conference would take place on December 10 and 11.

Israel has had strong economic ties with Turkey despite protests from some Arab states. The two countries have announced a bilateral free-trade agreement, which still needs parliamentary approval. There is also military cooperation between the two.
